conclusion: The pinned test asserts superseded spec text. Tint implements the current specification; changing it to pass would break conformance and the contradictory pinned staging test. No implementation can pass both pinned tests.

specification.FunctionDeclarationInstantiation: Let paramBindings be the list-concatenation of paramNames and « "arguments" ». Else, Let paramBindings be paramNames.
specification.B.3.2.1: If replacing the FunctionDeclaration funcDecl with a VariableStatement that has funcName as a BindingIdentifier would not produce any Early Errors for func and paramNames does not contain funcName, then ... If instantiatedVariableNames does not contain funcName and funcName is not "arguments", then [create var binding] ... When the FunctionDeclaration funcDecl is evaluated ... Perform ? funcEnv.SetMutableBinding(funcName, funcObj, false).
specification.reading: paramNames is the formals BoundNames only, so for a block function named arguments the binding creation is skipped but the evaluation-time copy still replaces the arguments object. The pinned test quotes the older text ("Append \"arguments\" to parameterNames").

nodeReference: Node v24.12.0 (V8): typeof arguments after the block is "function" for simple and rest parameters (matches current spec).
upstream: https://github.com/tc39/test262/pull/5112 (open): Correct block-decl-func-skip-arguments for the current FunctionDeclarationInstantiation
priorDecision: commit 077ab52d (native case for Annex B block functions named arguments) already documented this choice.
nextStep: Re-pin Test262 after upstream PR #5112 merges; the test should then pass unchanged.
